prompt:
The month-end settlement command is producing incorrect merchant payouts. Reproduce it with `python3 -m settlement data/sample.json --month 2025-03 --zone America/New_York`, investigate the modules, and repair the report (not the input data). Preserve that CLI and the public `settlement.report.build_report(document, month, zone)` API. Both return the same JSON-compatible dict; CLI prints one JSON line and exits 0 for valid input.

The document has `charges` (id, merchant, amount_cents, status, settled_at) and `refunds` (charge_id, amount_cents, posted_at) arrays. IDs of charges are unique. Amounts are nonnegative integers; timestamps are ISO-8601 with explicit offsets or Z. Pending charges may have settled_at=null. Inputs and month YYYY-MM and IANA zone are valid; no invalid-input behavior is required.

Count a charge's gross only if status is exactly 'settled' and its settled_at converted into the requested zone falls in the requested month. A refund counts in the month of its own posted_at in that zone, attributed using the referenced charge's merchant, even if that charge settled in a different month. Refunds referring to an unknown or non-settled charge are ignored. Multiple refunds all count, including refunds exceeding gross. Do not filter refund eligibility by the charge settlement month. Include a merchant if any eligible charge or refund occurs in the month, even if amounts or net are zero; exclude merchants with neither. Sort merchant names lexicographically. Return exactly {'month': month, 'zone': zone, 'merchants': [{'merchant': name, 'gross_cents': int, 'refund_cents': int, 'net_cents': gross-refund}, ...]}. Do not mutate the document. The sample's New York March report must contain Harbor (gross 10000, refunds 2500, net 7500) and Willow (gross 0, refunds 500, net -500), in that order. UTC March assigns the boundary charge differently. Add regression tests for the failure.
